key_insight: Increasing infrared pump intensity drives 2D (BA)₂PbI₄ from saturable to reverse saturable absorption, consistent with a Mott-like crossover from excitons to an electron–hole plasma.
engineering_relevance: The switchable nonlinear optical response could support infrared all-optical switching, although the abstract does not demonstrate solar-cell performance.
method: Femtosecond Z-scan measurements using a 1030 nm pump resonant with two-photon excitonic excitation.
Measure intensity-dependent nonlinear absorption and refractive response.
Probe carrier dynamics with transient absorption spectroscopy at matching excitation intensities.
evidence_signal: The absorption switch and a long-lived carrier population above the estimated Mott density jointly support the proposed intensity-driven Mott-like transition.
watch_item: The Mott density is estimated, and practical optical-device thresholds, stability, and integration remain unestablished in the abstract.
paper_title: Intensity-driven Mott-like transition in a 2D Ruddlesden-Popper perovskite
